title: New gateway routes must be added to the auth validator-lookup and gateway-disabled tests
answers: what tests do I update when I add a new gateway route?
why does my new gateway endpoint fail the static prefix validator test?
how do I verify a gateway route returns 501 when the gateway is disabled?
body:
Convention: gateway routes are listed in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_find_fastapi_validator_handles_static_prefix, both without and with STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR set, so the lookup via _find_fastapi_validator is verified for each route.
The disabled-gateway behavior is asserted in tests/server/test_gateway_disable.py:test_gateway_endpoints_return_501_when_disabled, which this PR extended with a GET call to the new route.
Skipping these leaves a route registered but unverified by the lookup test, or returning a non-501 status when disabled, without any test failing.
applies: Adding routes under gateway_router in mlflow/server/gateway_api.py.
says: Calling a new gateway endpoint returns an active response instead of being disabled.
Gateway endpoint authentication lookup fails when the server runs behind a static URL prefix.
Ensure newly created gateway endpoints are properly disabled when turning off the gateway.
Verify authentication validator routing for all newly added gateway endpoints under custom prefixes.
search: Adding routes under gateway_router in mlflow/server/gateway_api.py requires listing them in test_find_fastapi_validator_handles_static_prefix in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py and test_gateway_endpoints_return_501_when_disabled in tests/server/test_gateway_disable.py. The auth test verifies route lookup via _find_fastapi_validator both with and without STATIC_PREFIX_ENV_VAR set. The disabled test verifies that a GET call to the endpoint returns a 501 status when the gateway is disabled. Skipping these updates leaves routes untested for prefix validator lookup or returning non-501 statuses when disabled without test failures.
